steps.title: Prepare half‑strength TSB medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 15 g TSB powder in 1 L deionized water, autoclave 20 min at 121 °C, store at room temperature; for precultures prepare 250 mL (3.75 g TSB) in a separate bottle.

steps.title: Prepare full‑strength TSB agar (TSA)
steps.instruction: Mix 30 g TSB powder and 15 g agar per L deionized water; for 60 strains prepare 1.5 L (22.5 g TSB + 11.25 g agar in 750 mL per bottle, two bottles), autoclave 20 min at 121 °C and keep warm for pouring.

steps.title: Pour TSA into petri dishes
steps.instruction: Dispense ~25 mL of molten TSA into each sterile Ø 9 cm petri dish (Sarstedt, cat. 82.1473.001); prepare 60 plates and let dry 15 min with lids open in the sterile hood.

steps.title: Inoculate agar plates from glycerol stocks
steps.instruction: Using a sterile inoculation loop, scratch a small amount of cells from each glycerol stock tube, streak onto the corresponding TSA plate, allow any glycerol to dry, seal with parafilm; repeat for all 60 isolates.

steps.title: Incubate inoculated plates
steps.instruction: Place the inoculated plates in a 28 °C incubator for 4–10 days; ensure colonies are freshly growing and not too old for consistent precultures.

steps.title: Set up preculture deep‑well plates
steps.instruction: UV‑sterilize two 2 mL round‑bottom deep 96‑well plates (30 mm) for 15 min, then distribute three technical replicates of each bacterial isolate according to a predefined random layout; include two no‑bacteria controls (half‑strength TSB only) per plate, label plates with date and as “A” or “B”.

steps.title: Dispense half‑strength TSB into preculture wells
steps.instruction: Fill a sterile 50 mL reservoir with the half‑strength TSB prepared in step 1, then using an 8‑channel pipette transfer 1 mL of TSB into each well of the deep‑well plates.

steps.title: Transfer bacteria into preculture wells
steps.instruction: With a sterile inoculation needle, gently scratch a small amount of bacterial colony from the agar plate, dip the needle into the target well and stir until cells detach; tilt the deep‑well plate to improve visibility and avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Seal preculture plates with breathable foil
steps.instruction: Cover each deep‑well plate with a Breathe‑easy foil (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat. Z380059) to allow gas exchange while preventing contamination.

steps.title: Incubate precultures with shaking
steps.instruction: Place the sealed deep‑well plates on a laboratory shaker set to 28 °C and 180 rpm for 4 days.

steps.title: Make 100× chemical stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the test compound (e.g., MBOA, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat. 543551) in its appropriate solvent (e.g., DMSO, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat. D2438) to a final concentration of 500 mM (100× of the highest assay concentration); filter‑sterilize through a single‑use 0.20 µm filter compatible with the solvent.

steps.title: Prepare filter‑sterilized solvent control
steps.instruction: Filter‑sterilize >3 mL of the solvent (e.g., DMSO) that will serve as the solvent‑only control for all wells.

steps.title: Prepare half‑strength TSB for treatments
steps.instruction: Make 500 mL of half‑strength TSB (7.5 g TSB in 500 mL deionized water), autoclave as before; keep this bulk solution for dispensing into treatment tubes.

steps.title: Aliquot TSB into labeled centrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Label eight 50 mL centrifuge tubes with the intended final concentrations (0, 125, 250, 500, 750, 1250, 2500, 5000 µM) and add 45 mL of the half‑strength TSB to each.

steps.title: Create treatment solutions at target concentrations
steps.instruction: Add appropriate volumes of the 100× stock (500 mM) to each tube to reach the desired final concentrations: 0 µM (add solvent only), 125 µM (112.5 µL stock + 450 µL solvent), 250 µM (225 µL stock + 450 µL solvent), 500 µM (450 µL stock + 450 µL solvent), 750 µM (675 µL stock + 450 µL solvent), 1250 µM (1.125 mL stock + 450 µL solvent), 2500 µM (2.25 mL stock + 450 µL solvent), 5000 µM (450 µL stock + 450 µL solvent). Ensure each final treatment contains 450 µL solvent (1 % v/v). Prepare the solutions immediately before the stacker run; do not store.

steps.title: Create media control plate
steps.instruction: Fill a sterile 96‑well flat‑bottom plate (Corning, cat. 3595) with 200 µL half‑strength TSB per well using the 96‑channel pipetting system; discard any remaining TSB from the reservoir and clean the reservoir with 70 % ethanol followed by 15 min UV exposure.

steps.title: Add treatment solutions to stacker plates
steps.instruction: Using the 96‑channel pipette, sequentially load each treatment concentration into the corresponding stacker plates:

substeps.instruction: Load the lowest concentration solution into the reservoir, then dispense 196 µL into every well of stacker plate A; repeat for stacker plate B.
Replace the reservoir with the next higher concentration and repeat the 196 µL dispensing for both A and B plates.
Continue this process up to the highest concentration, always following the order from low to high.

steps.title: Discard used pipette tips
steps.instruction: After completing the dispensing of all treatment solutions, safely discard all used tips.

steps.title: Assemble treatment stacks (A and B)
steps.instruction: Arrange two separate stacks of plates: one containing all A‑stacker plates (one per concentration) and another containing all B‑stacker plates.

steps.title: Add bacterial precultures to stacker plates
steps.instruction: Change the 96‑channel pipette volume to 4 µL and load fresh tips:

substeps.instruction: From preculture plate A, remove the breathable foil, then pipette 4 µL of each well into the matching wells of the eight A‑stacker plates, starting with the lowest concentration and proceeding to the highest.
Discard the tips, load new tips, then repeat the same transfer from preculture plate B into the eight B‑stacker plates.

steps.title: Arrange plates in stack order
steps.instruction: Create a labellist.xlsx documenting the exact order of plates (including media control and empty plates at top and bottom); ensure the lowest plate (first to be read) is placed at the bottom of the stack and that all plates are oriented with well A1 at the top‑left corner.

steps.title: Load plates onto stacker input rack
steps.instruction: Place the ordered stack onto the input rack of the stacker, respecting the A1‑top‑left orientation, close the rack locks, and load the rack into the stacker instrument.

steps.title: Dispose of leftover bacterial material
steps.instruction: Discard any remaining liquid bacterial cultures according to biosafety waste disposal guidelines.

steps.title: Power on plate reader and stacker
steps.instruction: Turn on both the plate reader and the stacker device and verify they are properly connected.

steps.title: Configure Gen5 protocol settings
steps.instruction: Open the Gen5 software, load the provided protocol file (GrowthCurveOD600.prt), verify settings: read wavelength ≤600 nm, shake linear for 2 min before each read; enable “use stacker” and “plates have lids”, but do not tick “leave lids on during read”.

steps.title: Start stacker run
steps.instruction: Click the Start button in Gen5, then start the stacker; the instrument will remove lids, perform shaking, read OD600, and replace lids automatically.

steps.title: Run assay for 68 h
steps.instruction: Allow the stacker to run continuously for 68 hours (recommended maximum 72 h); periodically check for blockages, contamination in no‑bacteria controls, and evaporation.

steps.title: Stop run and export data
steps.instruction: After the desired time, press Stop (preferably after a full stack has been measured), select all plates in Gen5 and export the data as an Excel file.

steps.title: Discard plates with bacterial cultures
steps.instruction: Dispose of all plates containing liquid bacterial material according to biosafety regulations.

steps.title: Import raw growth data into R
steps.instruction: Load the exported Excel file (Sample_data_HT_Chem_Pheno.xlsx) and the metadata files Strain_Data.xlsx and labellist.xlsx into R; combine data from multiple runs if applicable.

steps.title: Normalize OD600 values
steps.instruction: Subtract the OD600 value of the first measurement from all subsequent time points for each well; calculate the maximal OD600 per well to identify poorly growing strains for possible exclusion.

steps.title: Plot growth curves
steps.instruction: Use the provided R script (HT_Chem_Pheno.rmd) to generate growth‑curve plots for individual wells, strains, or treatments to visually assess growth quality.

steps.title: Calculate AUC and normalized AUC
steps.instruction: Apply the auc() function from the MESS package to each well’s growth curve to obtain area‑under‑the‑curve (AUC); divide each treatment AUC by the AUC of the solvent control (0 µM) to obtain normalized AUC values.

steps.title: Compute tolerance index and IC50
steps.instruction: Calculate the tolerance index (TI) for each strain as the mean of its normalized AUCs across all concentrations; classify TI > 0.75 as tolerant, 0.5–0.75 as intermediate, <0.5 as susceptible. Optionally, use the same script to estimate IC50 (concentration causing 50 % growth inhibition) via the auc() function and log‑transform as described.
